title: LCBK19 harmonic quad grid for layout-figure rendering (deferred)
description: Lyon 2021 §6 ¶2 explicitly states that the dense quad mesh inside each layout patch is 'for visualization purposes' only, computed using [LCBK19, §6.2] (Lyon-Campen-Bommes-Kobbelt 2019, 'Parametrization quantization with free boundaries for trimmed quad meshing') — an optimized harmonic parametrization per patch with the 4 boundary side-edge counts as Dirichlet constraints. NOT the metriko visualizer (gen_qgp_*) approach we previously prototyped under PATCH-65/66/67/71. This ticket replaces or supersedes that work once PATCH-73 (conforming layout) lands. Algorithm sketch from LCBK19 §6.2: for each layout patch with side counts (n0, n1, n2, n3), build a target unit rectangle of size (n0, n1) (must equal (n2, n3) by consistency), solve a discrete harmonic map from the patch-region triangles to that rectangle with corner Dirichlet conditions, then extract a regular n0×n1 grid in (u,v) and lift back to 3D via barycentric inversion.
definition-of-done: On the conforming layout from PATCH-73, emit a watertight ArrayMesh with quads per patch matching Table-1 dense counts. Replaces metriko-visualizer SplitArcs/SplitArcTracer/IntersectionTable/QuadAssembler (those become deprecated/deletable).
testing-plan: Toy: 2x2 patch with edge counts (3,3,3,3) → 9 quads. Visual: render Hand-30k vs metriko hand-quad.obj, compare PNGs.
